items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1962-08-26
items.q: I guess I must have gotten the the love of it from hearing Joe Oliver on that cornet that he played on in 1917

ctx.x: I just wasn't exposed to the right people. They had them. Tom Brown was playing at that time and Tom Brown could always play well. But I just didn't hear them. The cornet players that I heard around town, I won't mention any names, but they played in the style which we called corny. To this day, people are still playing like that on the west coast. A lot of people are raving about those bands on the west coast. To me, it's still imitation jazz. It's corny. Well, they had many white cornet players that I heard…
Emmett Hardy, no. Some people you know rave about how... I have heard nothing but good about him.

items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1969-12-14
items.q: when I heard Joe Oliver I don't near passed out it was just too much for me

ctx.x: Well Dick let me start a little while before Joe Oliver so that you realize why I appreciated Joe Oliver so much. When I was a little boy there used to be a what they called a bottle man going through the streets collecting bottles from children you know the parents would store the bottles in the out rooms and the bottle man would go around and he had a long New Year's Eve noise making horn and in those days they built them pretty well I guess it was about two and a half feet long out of heavy tin as they called…

okay let's take a call because we have uh quite a few people uh interested in calling and discussing New Orleans jazz with one of the truly great Johnny Wiggs uh Johnny Wiggs and his New Orleans Kings we'll mention the names of the people in his band and I think you'll be uh surprised that some of the great names that not surprised certainly but uh people who tend to say oh yeah I forgot he used to play with with Johnny Wiggs and the New Orleans Kings we'll do that a little bit later on 523-2404 not the way you…
